v.rationale: All three share the same sound core: private local disk, hashed file names, a temporarySignedRoute with a 10-minute expiry, a signed unauthenticated download route, and 404 for a missing file at both link and download time. Content-sniffing validation rejected a PNG renamed .svg and an SVG with a script in all three. Differences are idiom plus one edge case: impl-1 and impl-2 store over-long client filenames unchanged (would 500 on MySQL strict varchar(255)); impl-3 truncates them, which avoids the error but drops the extension. impl-3 ranks first for the fluent File rule and route-level ->can() with a denyAsNotFound policy. impl-2 is nearly identical, with Gate::authorize, string rules and the most thorough tests. impl-1 is correct and the simplest but uses inline validation, a manual ownership check, and user_id in fillable, so it ranks last.
